name: gowalla-dataset-analysis
what_it_holds: Notebook/scripts for handling the Gowalla check-in dataset (Stanford SNAP social/location dataset, ~196K users, ~6.4M worldwide geotagged check-ins, 2009-2010). Repo processes the public dataset rather than shipping tourism-specific extracts; global coverage includes some Caribbean/Central American points of interest but they are not isolated.
why_useful: Global geotagged check-in data with lat/lon and time could in principle be turned into a travel/mobility-flow proxy (gap 20: party size/group travel/cross-border proxies via geotagged datasets), but the underlying SNAP dataset only covers 2009-2010, more than a decade before the ABNB forecast window, with no continuation - a historical curiosity, not a usable nowcast input.
license: none declared in this wrapper repo
themes: Twitter/X, Instagram, Flickr, TikTok tourism datasets: geotagged tourism flows, YFCC100M tourism subsets, Foursquare/Gowalla/Brightkite check-ins
Caribbean, Central America and island tourism stats (CTO, Costa Rica ICT, Dominican Republic BCRD, Bahamas, Puerto Rico) and Hawaii-like party-size / length-of-stay surveys
why_all: Global geotagged check-in data with lat/lon and time could in principle be turned into a travel/mobility-flow proxy (gap 20: party size/group travel/cross-border proxies via geotagged datasets), but the underlying SNAP dataset only covers 2009-2010, more than a decade before the ABNB forecast window, with no continuation - a historical curiosity, not a usable nowcast input.

Matches gap #20 (geotagged tourism datasets: Foursquare/Gowalla check-ins) as a worked example of loading/parsing the Gowalla check-in corpus, which could be re-mined for regional check-in density or trip length-of-stay proxies in island/Caribbean POIs if someone wanted to build that from the raw SNAP file.

name: gowalla-exp
what_it_holds: Trajectory-based analysis/experiment code over the same SNAP Gowalla check-in dataset described above; no new data, method/analysis scripts only.
why_useful: Same underlying 2009-2010 global check-in dataset as above; provides trajectory-extraction code that could be reused if a fresher check-in-style dataset were ever found, but stale on its own.
duplicate_of_holding: same source dataset as b00040611/gowalla-dataset-analysis above

why_all: Same underlying 2009-2010 global check-in dataset as above; provides trajectory-extraction code that could be reused if a fresher check-in-style dataset were ever found, but stale on its own.

Same rationale as gowalla-dataset-analysis: a second, slightly more developed (trajectory modeling) code path onto the Gowalla check-in corpus relevant to gap #20's geotagged mobility datasets; not island/Caribbean specific and needs substantial rework to extract a tourism-relevant series.

A second lead toward the raw(er) Gowalla check-in geodata (with trajectories, implying lat/lon/time preserved) rather than LightGCN's ID-only reduction; worth a closer read if the team wants a pre-2013 geotagged mobility panel as a structural (not current) party-size/cross-border proxy per gap #20.

A second, code-level example of how to turn raw Gowalla geotagged check-ins into trajectory/flow features, useful methods reference if a follow-up agent pursues the check-in-based tourist-flow idea above.

name: preprocessingDatasets
what_it_holds: Preprocessing scripts for both the Gowalla and Brightkite SNAP check-in datasets (Brightkite: ~4.5M check-ins, ~58k users, Apr 2008-Oct 2010, global). No data files committed, just cleaning/parsing code for the two external datasets.
why_useful: Convenience tooling for pulling in two of the classic geotagged social check-in corpora at once; both datasets are 2008-2010 vintage and stale for a 2026 nowcast, but the parsing code lowers the cost of exploring them if a team member wants a historical mobility baseline.
duplicate_of_holding: same two source datasets as the Gowalla repos above
